blocks.title: Adding
blocks.md: To **add** means to put together. 3 and 2 make 5. We write 3 + 2 = 5. The sign + means plus. The sign = means the same as.

blocks.caption: 4 and 3 more make 7.
blocks.alt: Four orange circles, a plus sign and three blue circles.

blocks.title: Count on
blocks.md: Start with the bigger number. Count on the smaller number. For 6 + 2: say six, then seven, eight. The answer is 8.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not count the first number again.
- Adding makes a bigger number.
- 0 added to a number does not change it.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps: Count on 3: seven, eight, nine. The answer is 9.

lessons.title: Taking away up to 10
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level I (Class 1) — Mathematics; to be checked against the official texts
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Take away from a small number.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Taking away
blocks.md: To **take away** is to make less. 5 take away 2 is 3. We write 5 − 2 = 3. The sign − means minus.

blocks.caption: 5 stars. If you take away 2 stars, 3 stars are left.
blocks.alt: Five yellow stars in a row.

blocks.title: Count back
blocks.md: Start at the big number. Count back the small number. For 7 − 2: say seven, then six, five. The answer is 5.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Taking away makes a smaller number.
- Do not count the number you start at.
- 4 − 0 is still 4.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps: Count back 4: eight, seven, six, five. The answer is 5.

lessons.title: Adding up to 20
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level I (Class 1) — Mathematics; to be checked against the official texts
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Add numbers with answers up to 20.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Make ten
blocks.md: To add 8 + 5, first make 10. 8 needs 2 more to be 10. Take 2 from the 5. Then 10 + 3 = 13.

blocks.caption: 8 and 5 make 13.
blocks.alt: Eight orange circles, a plus sign and five blue circles.

blocks.title: Steps
blocks.md: 1. Look at the big number. 2. How many make it 10? 3. Take that from the other number. 4. Add what is left to ten.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Count carefully when you go past 10.
- 9 + 4 is 13, not 12.
- Check with fingers or small stones.

lessons.title: Taking away up to 20
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level I (Class 1) — Mathematics; to be checked against the official texts
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Take away from numbers up to 20.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Take away from teens
blocks.md: To take away from 15, count back. 15 − 3: say fourteen, thirteen, twelve. The answer is 12.

blocks.caption: A number line from 10 to 20. The red dot is on 17.
blocks.alt: A number line with ticks from 10 to 20 and a red dot at 17.

blocks.title: Check by adding
blocks.md: Add the answer and the small number. 12 + 3 = 15. So 15 − 3 = 12 is right.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not forget to count back past 10.
- 13 − 4 is 9.
- Use the number line if you need it.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps: Count back 3: thirteen, twelve, eleven. The answer is 11.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps: Then take 2 more from 10. The answer is 8.

lessons.title: Story sums with adding and taking away
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level I (Class 1) — Mathematics; to be checked against the official texts
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Choose add or take away for a story.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: How to solve a story
blocks.md: 1. Read the story. 2. Is something added (more)? Or taken away (less)? 3. Do the sum. 4. Say the answer in a sentence.

blocks.caption: 5 pencils and 4 more.
blocks.alt: Five orange circles plus four blue circles.

blocks.title: Clue words
blocks.md: Words like **in all**, **together**, **more** tell us to add. Words like **left**, **give away**, **eat** tell us to take away.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not add when the story says *left*.
- Read the whole story first.
- Say the answer with its thing: 8 mangoes.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Bih has 5 pencils. Tanko gives her 4 more. How many pencils has Bih now?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A boy has 12 marbles. He gives 5 away. How many are left?
